title: The hypertrophy series: using strength work to control tonnage without sacrifice
summary: NH argues heavy compound strength work should open every session not mainly for strength but as a gauge: it accumulates tonnage fast, primes the body, and its performance tells you how recovered you are and how much accessory volume to do. Because it is a small share of total tonnage, it is also where cuts can be made without hurting the bodybuilding work.

claims.claim: Start training sessions with a heavy compound movement because it accumulates tonnage fast; bodybuilders should do heavy squats, deadlifts and bench.

The objection that deadlift tonnage is dispersed across too many muscles misses the point: compounds disperse tonnage quickly, fire up the body for what follows and show where the rest of the tonnage should go.
Strength work is not the most important part of his training; it is business as usual and the only part that never rotates: heavy deadlifts, squats, bench and curls are always there.
Heavy lifts give an accurate assessment of how recovered your body is.
Dropping strength work and training only in higher rep ranges slows progress (strength carries over to variations) and, worse, removes your gauge for how much volume to do.

If last session you squatted 300 lb for 4 and today only get 3, you regressed; that is a pre-emptive sign to do less volume that day, which you would miss if you went straight into fresh accessory volume.
Heavy sets don't have to be taxing; sometimes he piles volume on them, sometimes they just warm him up.
You can keep the strength-work weight constant and raise volume elsewhere to increase tonnage and drive leg hypertrophy.
Accessories and variations done in lower intensity windows are where he sculpts the body and targets details: the bodybuilding part of training, which suffers without strength work before it.
A small dose of strength work fires up the nervous system without tiring you, making the following accessories more efficient.

Because strength work is a small share of total tonnage, cuts made there barely affect weekly tonnage; it is the scapegoat for manipulation, whereas cutting accessories would remove too large a percentage.
Combine strength work as a gauge with lift rotation and evolving rep ranges and you get a program that never fails, with constant flexibility to keep progressing and stay consistent.
